title: Principled Design of Diffusion-based Optimizers for Inverse Problems
claim: Reparameterizing hyperparameters makes performance curves align across problem settings, enabling hyperparameter reuse and a better speed-quality tradeoff than competing solvers.
layout: 3x3 grid of line plots, top-to-bottom, standard vs ours rows, Pareto scatter bottom
description: A three-row grid of line plots. The top two rows have three columns, one for each hyperparameter: noise-schedule maximum (σ_max or τ_max), noise-schedule minimum (σ_min or τ_min), and sampler weight (λ or λ̂). Row labels on the left read 'Standard' and 'OptDiff'. Each plot shows normalized PSNR on the y-axis against the hyperparameter on a log x-axis. Colored curves stand for different settings: reconstruction versus deblurring configurations, added noise levels, or iteration intervals. In the Standard row the peaks are scattered and shifted. In the OptDiff row the curves collapse onto one aligned peak. A bottom row titled 'Faster inverse solvers' has three PSNR-versus-runtime plots for MRI, deblurring and super-resolution. Each plot has short line segments per method, and OptDiff in dark blue sits highest and furthest left. The eye goes first to the contrast between the scattered top-row curves and the aligned second-row curves.
caption: (Top) Comparison of standard and proposed hyperparameters for different experimental settings. Our proposed reparameterization ($\tau_{\max}, \tau_{\min})$ for noise schedule hyperparameters ($\sigma_{\max}, \sigma_{\min})$ produces aligned normalized PSNR curves across different inverse problem settings, showcasing invariance of OptDiff parameters. Similarly, our reparameterized sampler hyperparameter $\hat{\lambda}$ yields aligned curves for different iteration intervals, implying that a single $\hat{\lambda}$ value suffices during the entire reverse process in OptDiff. (Bottom) Performance comparisons between OptDiff and other diffusion-based inverse problem solvers. Our method OptDiff achieves the best runtime-PSNR tradeoff.
abstract: Score-based diffusion models achieve state-of-the-art performance for inverse problems, but their practical deployment is hindered by long inference times and cumbersome hyperparameter tuning. While pretrained diffusion models can be reused across tasks without retraining, inference-time hyperparameters such as the noise schedule and posterior sampling weights typically require ad-hoc adjustment for each problem setup. We propose principled reparameterizations that induce invariances, allowing the same hyperparameters to be reused across multiple problems without re-tuning. In addition, building on the RED-diff framework, which reformulates posterior sampling as an optimization problem, we further develop the OptDiff pipeline. OptDiff provides a simplified tuning framework that facilitates the integration of convex optimization tools to accelerate inference. Experiments on image reconstruction, deblurring, and super-resolution show substantial speedups and improved image quality.
